To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the μstp tailpiece of the μs heavy chain can function as a degronic retention signal that targets proteins for degradation by the endoplasmatic reticulum-associated degration (ERAD) pathway.
the μstp C-terminal tail of IgM μs functions both as a retention signal, preventing export from the endo-plasmic reticulm, and as an ER-associated degradation (ER-AD) degron.

μstp functions both as a retention signal, preventing the vesicular export of proteins from the endoplaspamic reticulum, and as a degradon, targeting the retained proteins for endoplasmic-reticulum-associated degradation, and that these functions are attributed to distinct elements in this C-terminal tailpiece of the immunoglobulin μ heavy chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism underlying protein quality control in the endoplamic reticulum.
the identification and characterization of the molecular determinants that govern the fate of aberrant proteins within the endoplasmatic reticulum and the secretory pathway.
understanding how the ERAD machinery is recruited to substrates and how this recruitment is regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cys residue is a necessary but not sufficient element for ERAD of a retained substrate, whereas the glycan is sufficient but not necessary for ERAD of the retained substrate.
the μstpCysteine acts as a retention signal, but that this is a consequence of a degron activity.
the μstpCYS motif acts as an ERAD retention signal and degron.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the μstpCysteine is the retention signal that is also required for the degradation of μstpCys fusions, but the N-glycans on the μstpCysts are not required for the retention and degradation.
μstp is a portable degrons that acts in ERAD by two mechanisms, the first of which involves a cysteine residue and a N-glycan, and the second of which involves the cysteine residue alone.
the C-terminal tailpiece of the μs heavy chain can be used both as a portable signal for protein retention in the endoplamic reticulum and as an ER-associated degradation signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the μstpCyt tailpiece can function as an ERAD signal in the absence of a ubiquitin-conjugating site, which suggests that the μstp motif may be a portable degronic element in the endoplaspic reticulum.
the μstpCYS motif can function as a retention signal or a degron in ERAD, but not as both in a single substrate.
the distinction between retention signals and degradation signals is not always clear, and the same sequence can function both as a signal for retention and for degradation.
